title: Two broadcasts tied at one instant for the fallback: the one whose first copy has the smaller delivery key is chosen
reasoning: Casey, issue #55 comment 7016583529, item 1: "PR #79, Q1 (tie at one instant): (a), the broadcast whose first copy has the smaller delivery key." lnk_02's fallback takes the position nearest in time, "the earlier on a tie"; ADR 0003 at bfe51aa times a broadcast by its first copy ("A broadcast's gateway copies count as one position, timed by the first copy, precise if any copy qualifies."). When two broadcasts are equally near and their first copies share an instant, Casey's (a) decides between them.

Broadcast B1, packet 56003, cell c20 at 20 bits: first copy c56-m003 at 23 10:00:00 (gateway c56-h1), later copy c56-m005 at 10:00:03 (c56-h2). Broadcast B2, packet 56004, cell D at 20 bits (1000.3 m north of c20 by stored values): first copy c56-m004 at 10:00:00 (c56-h1), later copy c56-m002 at 10:00:05 (c56-h2). Each pair shares node, packet id and stored values, so B1 and B2 are one position each, both timed 10:00:00. Every row is public only. The copies' gateways are not c56-g and the rows have no relay_node, so they are no receipts and make no candidate at c56-g.

The receipts are at 10:10, 10:15 and 10:20. Each look-back holds B1 (c20) and B2 (D), which neither overlap nor lie within 40 m, so c56-r is not stationary at any receipt and takes the 30-minute fallback (lnk_02, step 5). B1 and B2 are both 10, 15 and 20 minutes before the three receipts and are the only positions within 30 minutes: equally near, and equally early, at every receipt.

The tie goes to the broadcast whose first copy has the smaller delivery key: B1's first copy is c56-m003 and B2's is c56-m004, so B1 is chosen at every receipt and every relayer box is c20. c56-r has no hour box (not stationary) and each receipt keeps its own, all c20; c56-g is stationary on its 16-bit position of 22 09:00 at every receipt and on its hour box, g16. One box per end (step 8).

Reading the smallest key among all of a broadcast's copies instead would compare B1's c56-m003 with B2's c56-m002, a later copy, and choose B2: every relayer box would be D (3021.475856 m to g16) instead of c20. Reading each copy as its own position would choose c56-m002 at 10:00:05, nearer every receipt by 5 seconds, with the same box D.
relayer_precise_source is false: the covered cell c20 was read only in B1, whose copies are public. gateway_precise_source is false: c56-g's only cell has 16 bits and was sent on the public broker.

Every receipt is a direct hop (relay_node 21 is c56-r's own byte, lnk_01) and passes lnk_05 at 2745.603337 m from c20 to g16, boxes not overlapping. The hour has 3 packets: kept. Medians: SNR 5, 6 and 7 dB give 6.0; RSSI -90, -95 and -100 dBm give -95.0. position_uncertainty_m is c20's 22.734410 m plus g16's 363.750397 m, = 386.484807 m (lnk_05).
